boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Cal Poly Pomona traditions, from its student-built Rose Parade float and pumpkin harvest to Bronco-specific welcome rituals and recurring campus celebrations.

cards.title: Build a Rose Parade Float from Scratch
cards.subtitle: Cal Poly Pomona and Cal Poly San Luis Obispo’s student-built parade tradition
cards.notes: Follow the student team’s yearlong design, construction and floral-decoration process, then look for the completed float in Pasadena.
cards.short_summary: Students from the two Cal Poly campuses have created a Rose Parade float together since 1949.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly Pomona identifies the Rose Float as one of its most storied traditions, dating to 1949, and says its student team prepares the Rose Parade’s only student-built float.
cards.source_title: Rose Float Experience is Unlike Any Other
cards.access_notes: Construction participation and public viewing opportunities vary by season; consult the Rose Float Program before visiting.

cards.title: Pick a Student-Grown Pumpkin
cards.subtitle: An October agricultural tradition at Kellogg Ranch
cards.notes: Visit during the announced October dates to explore the pumpkin field and agricultural attractions; buy admission in advance when advised.
cards.short_summary: The university’s fall festival centers on thousands of pumpkins grown and harvested through its agricultural program.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly Pomona’s 2025 announcement calls Pumpkin Festival an annual Pomona Valley tradition, marks its 32nd year and documents 30,000 student-grown pumpkins.
cards.source_title: Cal Poly Pomona Pumpkin Festival Opens Oct. 4
cards.access_notes: Seasonal ticketed event at Kellogg Ranch; confirm the current October schedule, admission and parking instructions before traveling.

cards.title: Join the Campus-Wide Hot Dog Caper
cards.subtitle: A free-lunch welcome tradition dating to 1983
cards.notes: Watch for the fall announcement, then head to Bronco Commons for the themed lunch, entertainment and campus-resource booths.
cards.short_summary: Hundreds of volunteers distribute hot dogs, snacks and drinks at CPP’s large annual welcome-back gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: The university documented the 42nd annual Hot Dog Caper in 2025, featuring free hot dogs, chips, drinks and popsicles with support from more than 200 volunteers.
cards.source_title: Hot Dog Caper Returns for Magical 42nd Anniversary
cards.access_notes: Recurring campus event for students, staff and faculty; confirm the next date and eligibility in the current university announcement.

cards.title: Kick Off the Year at BroncoFusion
cards.subtitle: CPP’s annual student concert at Bronco Commons
cards.notes: Secure the required ticket and wristband, bring approved identification and review the clear-bag and prohibited-item rules before entry.
cards.short_summary: Student performers and a headlining act open the academic year with a concert staged directly on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI’s official page describes BroncoFusion as a mega-concert that kicks off Cal Poly Pomona’s academic year with student performances and headlining acts.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the 2026 event for August 21 at 7:30–11 p.m.; admission requires a ticket, wristband and qualifying identification.

cards.title: Turn Basketball Day Green and Gold
cards.subtitle: A young Bronco Commons tradition paired with a basketball doubleheader
cards.notes: Wear school colors, start at the Bronco Commons festivities and reserve game tickets if the current announcement requests an RSVP.
cards.short_summary: CPP combines family-friendly carnival activities with women’s and men’s basketball games in one school-color celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: The university documented its third annual Green & Gold Block Party in 2026 as a free Bronco Commons event followed by a women’s and men’s basketball doubleheader with free admission.
cards.source_title: CPP to Host Third Annual Green and Gold Block Party
cards.access_notes: The January 31, 2026 edition and both games were free; check the next annual announcement for RSVP and ticket procedures.

cards.title: Take a Finals Break at Midnight Madness
cards.subtitle: ASI’s semesterly Bronco Student Center takeover
cards.notes: Check ASI’s event listing one or two Fridays before finals and register when required for the announced theme and activities.
cards.short_summary: The Bronco Student Center becomes a themed late-semester recreation night designed as a study break.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI describes Midnight Madness as a semesterly event held one to two Fridays before finals, transforming the Bronco Student Center with themed activities and free food.
cards.source_title: Special Events - ASI Cal Poly Pomona
cards.access_notes: The recurring timing is documented, but a current event date and closing time are not posted on the source page; verify before attending.

cards.title: Cosplay at CPP’s Own Convention
cards.subtitle: A Bronco-focused campus convention for comics, anime and creative hobbies
cards.notes: Review the year’s registration details, then plan around workshops, the artist-vendor area, cosplay contest and closing guest session.
cards.short_summary: CPP’s in-house convention gathers students around pop culture, creative skills, cosplay and a guest question-and-answer session.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI documents BroncoCon as CPP’s convention for Bronco hobby communities, featuring workshops, a vendor and artist area, a cosplay contest and a concluding celebrity Q&A.
cards.source_title: Special Events - ASI Cal Poly Pomona
cards.access_notes: Registration is referenced, but the source page does not provide a current date, eligibility rules or admission price; verify with ASI.

cards.title: Leave the Next Class Something Useful
cards.subtitle: A graduating-class tradition that began with campus carillons in 1966
cards.notes: Explore the philanthropy map, review the current class project and contribute only through the university’s official giving channel.
cards.short_summary: Each graduating class can collectively fund a project intended to improve campus life for future Broncos.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP calls the Class Gift one of its oldest traditions, says it began in 1966 with donated carillons and documents a new collective project selected each spring.
cards.access_notes: Participation involves an optional charitable contribution; use the current official page for the selected project and donation terms.

cards.title: Welcome a New Bronco with a Pin
cards.subtitle: A peer-to-peer ritual during New Student Convocation
cards.notes: Attend the official convocation program, receive the Broncos Belong enamel pin and follow the ceremony’s directions for peer pinning.
cards.short_summary: New students pin one another during convocation as a formal welcome into the Bronco community.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP’s account of its inaugural New Student Convocation says every student received a Broncos Belong enamel pin and students pinned one another during the ceremony.
cards.source_title: Cal Poly Pomona Hosts Inaugural New Student Convocation to Foster Belonging and Sense of Pride
cards.access_notes: This is a new-student convocation activity; attendance and participation instructions are set by the university for each incoming class.

cards.title: Toss a Painted Horseshoe for Bronco Luck
cards.subtitle: A new convocation ritual at the Bronco statue
cards.notes: If offered at convocation, paint the provided wooden horseshoe and toss it only from the supervised event area near the statue.
cards.short_summary: Incoming students aim decorated wooden horseshoes toward the Bronco statue’s hooves as a playful luck ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP identifies the painted wooden horseshoe toss as a new tradition introduced at the 2024 convocation, with closer throws to the Bronco statue’s hooves associated with better luck.
cards.source_title: Cal Poly Pomona Hosts Inaugural New Student Convocation to Foster Belonging and Sense of Pride
cards.access_notes: Documented as a new supervised convocation activity in 2024; verify that it remains in the current new-student program.
